questions.topic: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana
questions.subtopic: Crowding-out effect of deficit-financed government borrowing
questions.stem: A government finances a larger fiscal deficit by issuing additional bonds. If the supply of private savings does not increase, which outcome describes the standard crowding-out channel?
options: Private investment may fall as government borrowing competes for available savings and pushes interest rates upward.
Private investment must rise because government bonds add directly to firms' retained earnings.
The fiscal deficit automatically turns into a current-account surplus.
Interest rates are forced to zero because government bonds are risk-free.
explanations: Correct. In the standard crowding-out mechanism, additional government borrowing competes for available savings; upward pressure on interest rates can reduce private borrowing and investment.
Government bonds are liabilities issued to finance public borrowing; they do not automatically become firms' retained earnings.
A fiscal deficit and the current-account balance are different measures; one does not automatically determine the other.
Government borrowing does not force interest rates to zero; it may put upward pressure on rates when funds are constrained.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: Economic and Social Development of India and Telangana; NCERT Class XII Introductory Macroeconomics, Chapter 5, Government Budget and the Economy (crowding-out discussion), SATHEE-IITK: https://sathee.iitk.ac.in/sathee-cuet/student-corner/ncert-books/class-12/economics/introductory-to-macroeconomics/chapter-05-government-budget-and-the-economy/

questions.subtopic: Counting binary relations on a finite set
questions.stem: A set A contains 3 elements. How many different binary relations can be defined on A?
explanations: Nine is the number of ordered pairs in A × A, not the number of possible relations.
Sixty-four counts the reflexive relations on a three-element set; the question allows every binary relation, including non-reflexive ones.
Correct. A binary relation is any subset of A × A. There are 3 × 3 = 9 ordered pairs, and each pair can independently be included or excluded, giving 2⁹ = 512 relations.
729 is 3⁶ and does not count the subsets of the nine possible ordered pairs.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Set Theory & Algebra; Linear Algebra; Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, section on relations (a relation on A is a subset of A × A); independent count: 2^(3×3) = 512.

questions.topic: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic
questions.subtopic: Ordinary generating function for the sequence a_n = n
questions.stem: For the sequence aₙ = n for n ≥ 0, which expression is its ordinary generating function A(x) = Σₙ≥₀ aₙxⁿ?
options: x divided by (1 minus x) squared
1 divided by (1 minus x)
1 divided by (1 minus x) squared
x divided by (1 plus x) squared
explanations: Correct. Differentiating 1/(1 − x) = Σₙ≥₀ xⁿ and multiplying by x gives Σₙ≥₀ n xⁿ = x/(1 − x)², for |x| < 1.
1/(1 − x) is the generating function for the constant sequence 1, 1, 1, …, not 0, 1, 2, 3, ….
1/(1 − x)² generates 1, 2, 3, 4, …; its coefficient of xⁿ is n + 1.
The plus sign produces an alternating-sign pattern and is not the generating function for aₙ = n.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Combinatorics and Discrete Structures; Graph Theory; Mathematical Logic; Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications, generating functions; identity derived from the geometric series for |x| < 1.

questions.subtopic: Write-invalidate cache coherence in shared-memory multiprocessors
questions.stem: In a write-invalidate cache-coherence protocol, two processors hold the same cache block in the Shared state. Processor P1 wants to write to that block. Which action is required before P1 can safely modify its cached copy?
options: P1 broadcasts an invalidation so other shared copies become invalid before P1 writes.
P1 writes locally while all other Shared copies remain valid.
P1 sends the updated data to every cache without invalidating any copy.
P1 discards its copy and waits for another processor to perform the write.
explanations: Correct. A write-invalidate protocol invalidates other cached copies of the block so the writing processor can obtain exclusive write ownership and preserve coherence.
Leaving other Shared copies valid would allow processors to read stale data after P1 modifies its copy.
Sending updated data to all copies is a write-update approach, not a write-invalidate approach.
The protocol does not require the writer to wait for another processor; it requests ownership and invalidates other copies.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Organization and Architecture (multiprocessors and cache); Cornell University CS3410, Cache Coherency: https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs3410/2025fa/notes/cachecoherency.html; INFLIBNET e-content, Cache Coherence I: https://ebooks.inflibnet.ac.in/csp2/chapter/cache-coherence-i/

questions.subtopic: Queue implemented with two stacks: amortized complexity
questions.stem: A FIFO queue is implemented using two stacks. Enqueue pushes onto an input stack; dequeue transfers all input items to an output stack only when the output stack is empty. What is the amortized time per queue operation over a sequence of m operations?
options: O(log n)
O(n)
O(n²)
explanations: Correct. Each item is pushed onto the input stack once, transferred to the output stack at most once, and popped once. Thus a sequence of m queue operations takes O(m) total time, or O(1) amortized per operation.
The implementation does not perform a logarithmic search or tree operation; stack operations are constant time.
A single dequeue can take O(n) when it transfers many items, but this is not the amortized cost per operation over the whole sequence.
Each item is moved only a constant number of times, so the total work is linear rather than quadratic.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming and Data Structures; Cornell University CS312, Amortized Algorithms, queue using two stacks: https://www.cs.cornell.edu/courses/cs312/2007fa/lectures/lec20.html; Princeton COS 226, Stacks and Queues: https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/spring21/cos226/lectures/study/13StacksAndQueues.html

questions.subtopic: Paging: internal fragmentation in the final page
questions.stem: A process requires 10 KiB of memory and the operating system uses 4 KiB pages. If the process is allocated the minimum whole number of pages, how much space is wasted inside its allocated pages?
options: 2 KiB of internal fragmentation
2 KiB of external fragmentation
4 KiB of internal fragmentation
10 KiB of internal fragmentation
explanations: Correct. Three pages allocate 12 KiB. The process uses 10 KiB, leaving 2 KiB unused inside its final allocated page; this is internal fragmentation.
The unused space is inside an allocated page, not a gap between separate free memory blocks; it is internal fragmentation.
The process needs three 4 KiB pages, so the allocated capacity is 12 KiB and the waste is 12 − 10 = 2 KiB, not 4 KiB.
The process uses 10 KiB of the 12 KiB allocated; only the remaining 2 KiB is unused.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Operating Systems; INFLIBNET e-content, Memory Management – Paging I, section 21.2.3 Fragmentation: https://ebooks.inflibnet.ac.in/csp3/chapter/memory-management-paging-i/

questions.subtopic: WTO national treatment under GATT Article III
questions.stem: An imported water pump has cleared customs and is like a domestically manufactured pump. Under the WTO's GATT Article III national-treatment rule, which measure would generally violate the principle?
options: Charging the imported pump a higher internal tax than the like domestic pump.
Applying the same internal tax rate to imported and like domestic pumps.
Applying a customs tariff at the border within the member's bound rate.
Applying the same internal safety standard to imported and domestic pumps.
explanations: Correct. National treatment under GATT Article III prevents imported like products from being subjected to higher internal taxes than domestic like products.
Equal internal tax treatment is consistent with national treatment, assuming the products are like and the measure is otherwise compliant.
A customs tariff collected at the border is not the internal-tax comparison tested by Article III; tariff commitments are a separate issue.
An internal safety standard applied equally to imported and domestic like products does not, on that fact alone, breach national treatment.

questions.topic: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology
questions.subtopic: Zener diode reverse-breakdown voltage regulation
questions.stem: A 6.2 V Zener diode is connected in reverse bias across a load, with a series resistor. If the supply voltage rises slightly while the diode remains within its specified current and power limits, what is the expected output?
options: It remains approximately 6.2 V; the Zener current adjusts to absorb the change.
It rises by exactly the same amount as the supply.
It falls to approximately 0.7 V because the diode is reverse biased.
It becomes zero because reverse bias prevents all current in breakdown.
explanations: Correct. In its designed reverse-breakdown region, a Zener diode holds its terminal voltage approximately at its Zener voltage; the series resistor limits current and the Zener current changes.
A regulated output does not track a small supply increase one-for-one while the Zener remains in regulation.
About 0.7 V is a typical forward drop for a silicon diode, not the regulated reverse-breakdown voltage of this 6.2 V Zener.
A Zener is designed to conduct in its reverse-breakdown region; it does not block all current there.
questions.basis: Official Paper I syllabus: General Science; India’s Achievements in Science and Technology. Electronics Textbook, Zener diodes and reverse-breakdown voltage regulation: https://www.allaboutcircuits.com/textbook/semiconductors/chpt-3/zener-diodes/

questions.subtopic: Indian Ocean Dipole: positive-phase sea-surface-temperature pattern
questions.stem: Which sea-surface-temperature pattern characterises a positive phase of the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)?
options: Warmer-than-normal western equatorial Indian Ocean and cooler-than-normal eastern equatorial Indian Ocean.
Cooler-than-normal western equatorial Indian Ocean and warmer-than-normal eastern equatorial Indian Ocean.
Simultaneous warming across the entire equatorial Indian Ocean with no east–west gradient.
A warm central Pacific and cool eastern Pacific, with no Indian Ocean anomaly.
explanations: Correct. A positive IOD is characterised by warmer-than-normal sea-surface temperatures in the western tropical Indian Ocean and cooler-than-normal temperatures in the eastern tropical Indian Ocean.
This is the opposite east–west anomaly pattern, associated with a negative IOD.
A dipole requires an east–west contrast; uniform warming does not describe its positive phase.
This describes a Pacific Ocean pattern, not the Indian Ocean Dipole.

questions.subtopic: Amortized analysis of stack MULTIPOP operations
questions.stem: An initially empty stack supports PUSH, POP and MULTIPOP. For any sequence of n such operations, what is the general upper bound on total work, and hence the amortized work per operation?
options: O(n) total; O(1) amortized per operation.
O(n²) total; O(n) amortized per operation.
O(n log n) total; O(log n) amortized per operation.
O(1) total; O(1/n) amortized per operation.
explanations: Correct. Each element is pushed at most once and can be popped at most once, including through MULTIPOP, so the total number of stack-element operations is O(n).
A single MULTIPOP can cost O(n), but elements cannot be popped repeatedly after they have been removed; the whole sequence is not O(n²).
There is no necessary logarithmic factor: charging each pop to its earlier push gives a linear total bound.
A sequence containing n operations necessarily has at least linear total operation overhead; it cannot have O(1) total work.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Algorithms; amortized analysis and worst-case time complexity. Princeton/Kleinberg–Tardos lecture notes, Multipop stack aggregate method: https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~wayne/kleinberg-tardos/pdf/AmortizedAnalysis.pdf

questions.subtopic: Nondeterministic PDA acceptance by final state versus empty stack
questions.stem: For nondeterministic pushdown automata (NPDAs), which statement about acceptance by final state and acceptance by empty stack is correct?
options: Acceptance by empty stack is strictly more powerful.
Both modes recognise exactly the same class of languages; an equivalent NPDA can be constructed.
Acceptance by final state recognises only regular languages.
The two modes are equivalent only when the PDA has no epsilon-transitions.
explanations: Incorrect. Neither acceptance mode is more powerful for NPDAs; each can simulate the other.
Correct. For NPDAs, acceptance by final state and acceptance by empty stack are equivalent in language-recognition power.
Incorrect. NPDAs accepting by final state can recognise context-free languages, including non-regular ones.
Incorrect. The equivalence theorem does not require eliminating all epsilon-transitions from the original PDA.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Theory of Computation; context-free languages and push-down automata. Columbia University, PDA acceptance modes: https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~aho/cs3261/Lectures/L8-PDA.html

questions.subtopic: Safety of tuple relational calculus expressions
questions.stem: A tuple relational calculus (TRC) expression is syntactically valid but can return tuples containing values that occur in neither the database relations nor the constants referenced by the formula. What is the problem with this expression?
options: It is unsafe because its result may be infinite or depend on values outside the active domain.
It is invalid because tuple relational calculus cannot use negation.
It violates first normal form because tuple variables contain attributes.
It is not relationally complete because it cannot be translated into SQL.
explanations: Correct. An unsafe TRC expression can produce an infinite or domain-dependent result; a safe expression restricts result values to the domain of the formula.
TRC permits logical negation; safety restrictions address the range of values and finiteness, not a blanket ban on negation.
First normal form concerns relation attributes and values, not the safety condition for a TRC query expression.
Safe TRC has the same expressive power as relational algebra; the issue described is safety, not relational completeness.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Databases; relational model and tuple relational calculus. Silberschatz, Korth and Sudarshan, Database System Concepts, Chapter 27, Safety of Expressions: https://codex.cs.yale.edu/avi/db-book/online-chapters-dir/27.pdf

questions.subtopic: Digital signatures: private-key signing and public-key verification
questions.stem: A sender digitally signs a document using its private key, and a recipient verifies the signature using the corresponding public key. Which security property is not supplied by the digital-signature operation alone?
options: Integrity of the signed data.
Evidence supporting origin authentication.
Support for signer non-repudiation.
Confidentiality of the document contents.
explanations: A valid digital signature supports integrity by allowing the recipient to detect alteration of the signed data.
A valid signature verified with the signer's trusted public key supports authentication of the signed origin.
Digital signatures provide support for signer non-repudiation, subject to sound key management and implementation.
Correct. A digital signature does not hide the document contents; confidentiality requires encryption or another confidentiality mechanism.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Computer Networks; public/private key cryptography and digital signature. NIST CSRC, Digital Signature glossary: https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/digital_signature

questions.subtopic: JSP JspContext.findAttribute scope-search order
questions.stem: In a JSP page, the same attribute name `theme` exists in request and session scope, but not in page scope. What does `pageContext.findAttribute("theme")` return?
options: The value from session scope, because session lasts longer.
The value from request scope, because it is searched before session scope.
The value from application scope, because it is global.
null, because findAttribute searches only page scope.
explanations: Incorrect. Session scope is searched after request scope, so it does not win when the name already exists in request scope.
Correct. JspContext.findAttribute searches page, request, session and application scopes in that order; request is the first matching scope here.
Incorrect. Application scope is searched after request and session scopes.
Incorrect. getAttribute(name) checks page scope only; findAttribute(name) searches all four scopes in order.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Web Technologies; Servlets and JSP. Jakarta Server Pages API, JspContext.findAttribute method: https://jakarta.ee/specifications/pages/3.0/apidocs/jakarta/servlet/jsp/JspContext.html

questions.subtopic: DBSCAN core-point criterion and min_samples
questions.stem: A DBSCAN run uses `min_samples = 5`. Under the standard definition, how many samples must lie in a point's `eps`-neighbourhood for it to qualify as a core point?
options: At least five samples, including the point itself.
At least five other samples, excluding the point itself.
Exactly five clusters must be within `eps`.
Any number, provided the point is closest to a centroid.
explanations: Correct. The DBSCAN core-sample definition counts the point itself as part of its `eps`-neighbourhood, so at least five samples in total are required here.
Incorrect. The point itself is included in the standard `min_samples` count.
Incorrect. `min_samples` is a neighbourhood sample count, not a count of clusters.
Incorrect. DBSCAN is density-based and does not assign points by distance to a centroid.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Data Mining; clustering algorithms. Scikit-learn user guide, DBSCAN core-sample definition: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html#dbscan

questions.subtopic: ICC complementarity under Rome Statute Article 17
questions.stem: Under Article 17 of the Rome Statute, which circumstance can make a case admissible before the ICC despite domestic proceedings?
options: The State with jurisdiction is unwilling or unable genuinely to investigate or prosecute the case.
The domestic court is located outside the country's capital.
The accused disagrees with a national court's decision and files an ordinary appeal to the ICC.
The alleged offence has affected citizens of more than one country.
explanations: Correct. Under Article 17, a case may be admissible when the State with jurisdiction is unwilling or unable genuinely to carry out the investigation or prosecution, subject to the Statute's other admissibility requirements.
The location of a domestic court does not determine ICC admissibility under the complementarity principle.
The ICC is not an ordinary appellate court for national criminal judgments.
Cross-border effects alone do not establish admissibility; the Rome Statute's jurisdiction and admissibility conditions still apply.

questions.subtopic: C11 volatile qualifier versus atomic synchronization
questions.stem: Two C11 threads access a shared `volatile int flag`; one writes while the other reads, without an atomic operation or a lock. Which statement is correct?
options: The volatile qualifier makes every read and write indivisible, so the access is automatically thread-safe.
The volatile qualifier creates a release/acquire synchronizes-with relationship between the threads.
The volatile qualifier alone provides neither atomicity nor inter-thread synchronization; use a C atomic object or a mutex for thread-safe communication.
The volatile qualifier automatically orders all ordinary memory accesses made by both threads.
explanations: Incorrect. C's volatile qualifier does not promise indivisible accesses; atomicity must come from an atomic type or another synchronization mechanism.
Incorrect. C volatile does not create a release/acquire synchronizes-with relationship between threads.

Correct. In C11, volatile affects treatment of accesses but does not itself make them atomic or establish inter-thread synchronization. Conflicting unsynchronized non-atomic accesses can constitute a data race; use `_Atomic` operations or a mutex.
Incorrect. Volatile does not impose a global ordering on ordinary non-volatile memory accesses across threads.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Programming in C. SEI CERT C CON02-C, Do not use volatile as a synchronization primitive: https://cmu-sei.github.io/secure-coding-standards/sei-cert-c-coding-standard/recommendations/concurrency-con/con02-c/ ; WG14 N1479, C atomic versus volatile rationale: https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n1479.htm

questions.subtopic: Loop unrolling as a compiler code-optimisation technique
questions.stem: An optimizing compiler duplicates a loop body several times within one iteration so that fewer loop-control branches are executed. Which optimization is being applied?
options: Loop unrolling.
Loop-invariant code motion.
Strength reduction.
Dead-code elimination.
explanations: Correct. Loop unrolling replicates the loop body and adjusts the iteration step, reducing loop-control overhead at the possible cost of increased code size.
Loop-invariant code motion moves computations that do not change across iterations outside the loop; it does not primarily duplicate the body.
Strength reduction replaces an expensive operation with a cheaper equivalent operation, often inside a loop.
Dead-code elimination removes computations whose results are not needed; it does not replicate loop iterations.
questions.basis: Official Paper II syllabus: Compiler Design; basics of code optimisation. LLVM documentation, Analysis and Transform Passes, `loop-unroll`: https://www.llvm.org/docs/Passes.html

questions.subtopic: UML sequence diagrams: meaning and notation of a lifeline
questions.stem: In a UML sequence interaction, what is the name of the vertical dashed line that descends from a participant's head?
options: Lifeline.
Activation bar (execution specification).
Message arrow.
